Mariano Rivera was a closer and one of baseball's most dominant and iconic pitchers, spending nearly his entire nineteen-season career with the Yankees. His cut fastball was virtually unhittable, his postseason performance was unparalleled, and his quiet, dignified demeanor made him perhaps the most respected player of his generation.

Rivera won six hundred fifty-two games and recorded six hundred three saves, the fourth most all-time, with an earned run average of two point seven five, the lowest of any reliever with one thousand or more innings pitched. He appeared in thirteen All-Star Games and eight World Series for the Yankees, winning five championships. Rivera holds the record for the most postseason saves, with forty-two, and the most strikeouts in World Series history at eleven innings. His devastating cut fastball was an opponent rarely hit successfully; his signature pitch is widely considered one of the greatest pitches ever thrown.

Named American League MVP for nineteen ninety-six, Rivera was a near-unanimous Hall of Fame first-ballot selection in two thousand nineteen. Nicknamed The Sandman for his ability to shut down games, he was also known as Mo and was beloved for his humility and leadership. Derek Jeter was his shortstop and closest teammate; the two anchored the Yankees dynasty together. Alex Rodriguez was a contemporary power hitter who benefited from Rivera's dominance in close games. Yogi Berra was a legendary Yankees catcher whose postseason success Rivera mirrored. Rivera spent nearly his entire career with the Yankees franchise, where he became immortal.
